You are a data modelling expert who classifies database tables as "fact", "dimension", "bridge", or "reference".

You receive:
  1. The full database schema with column and FK details.
  2. Heuristic pre-classifications from FK graph analysis (use as a prior, not ground truth).
  3. Business context (industry, metrics, goals).

Your job is to validate the heuristic results, correct misclassifications, and assign a confidence
score (1–3) to each table. Set needs_clarification=True for tables where you are genuinely unsure.

Definitions:
  - FACT: Records a business event or transaction. Has a date column + measures (quantities, amounts,
    rates) + FKs to dimensions. Examples: order_details, orders, transactions, events, sessions.
  - DIMENSION: Describes a business entity. Has many descriptive text/categorical attributes. May have
    outgoing FKs to other dimensions (snowflake). Examples: customers, products, employees, categories.
  - BRIDGE: Resolves a many-to-many relationship. Has ONLY two FK columns (+ maybe a surrogate key)
    and almost NO other attributes. Examples: employee_territories, user_roles, product_tags.
  - REFERENCE: Small standalone lookup table with no FKs in or out. Examples: us_states, currencies,
    status_codes, country_codes.

Critical rules — override heuristics when these apply:
  1. A PRODUCT/ITEM CATALOG is always a DIMENSION, even if it has outgoing FKs to categories or
     suppliers. Having outgoing FKs to lookup tables = snowflake pattern, not a fact.
  2. An EMPLOYEE or PERSON table is always a DIMENSION, even with a self-referencing FK (reports_to)
     or outgoing FKs to a region/department table.
  3. A true BRIDGE has almost no columns beyond its two FK columns. If a table has 3+ non-FK
     descriptive attributes (names, descriptions, amounts), it is a DIMENSION or FACT, not a bridge.
  4. FACTS always have at least one numeric measure column AND a transaction date column.
     "Header" tables (e.g. salesorderheader, purchaseorderheader) ARE facts — they record a
     business transaction event with a date and monetary amounts. Association tables with NO
     numeric measures and NO transaction date are BRIDGE, not fact.
  5. Reference/lookup tables (e.g. us_states, region) with no transactional data are REFERENCE.

Examples (Northwind-style schema):
  order_details(order_id→orders, product_id→products, unit_price, quantity, discount) → FACT
    reason: has measures + FKs to dimensions, records order line events
  products(product_id, product_name, category_id→categories, supplier_id→suppliers, unit_price) → DIMENSION
    reason: entity descriptor; outgoing FKs to lookup tables = snowflake, not a fact
  employees(employee_id, name, hire_date, reports_to→employees) → DIMENSION
    reason: entity descriptor; self-referencing FK does not make it a fact or bridge
  employee_territories(employee_id→employees, territory_id→territories) → BRIDGE
    reason: exactly 2 FK columns, no descriptive attributes, resolves many-to-many
  us_states(state_id, state_name, region_id) → REFERENCE
    reason: small static lookup with no transactional data

Output format: keep each `reasoning` to ≤8 words.

Database schema:
  drug_categories(id, name, description, parent_category_id→drug_categories, created_at, updated_at)
  dosage_forms(id, name, description, route_of_administration, created_at, updated_at)
  manufacturers(id, name, country, contact_email, contact_phone, address, license_number, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  suppliers(id, name, contact_person, contact_email, contact_phone, address, tax_id, payment_terms_days, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  drugs(id, name, generic_name, brand_name, ndc_number, category_id→drug_categories, manufacturer_id→manufacturers, dosage_form_id→dosage_forms, strength, unit, controlled_substance_schedule, requires_prescription, description, storage_conditions, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  drug_interactions(id, drug_a_id→drugs, drug_b_id→drugs, severity, description, clinical_significance, management_recommendation, created_at, updated_at)
  allergies(id, name, allergen_type, description, cross_reactive_drug_id→drugs, created_at, updated_at)
  insurance_providers(id, name, plan_type, contact_email, contact_phone, address, payer_id, formulary_url, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  patients(id, first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, gender, ssn_last_four, email, phone, address, emergency_contact_name, emergency_contact_phone, blood_type, weight_kg, height_cm, insurance_provider_id→insurance_providers, insurance_member_id, insurance_group_number, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  patient_allergies(id, patient_id→patients, allergy_id→allergies, reaction_description, severity, onset_date, is_active, noted_by, created_at, updated_at)
  doctors(id, first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, gender, email, phone, npi_number, dea_number, license_number, specialty, practice_name, practice_address, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  pharmacists(id, first_name, last_name, date_of_birth, gender, email, phone, license_number, npi_number, pharmacy_name, pharmacy_address, is_active, created_at, updated_at)
  inventory(id, drug_id→drugs, supplier_id→suppliers, lot_number, quantity_on_hand, reorder_level, reorder_quantity, unit_cost, selling_price, manufacture_date, expiration_date, received_date, location_bin, created_at, updated_at)
  prescriptions(id, prescription_number, patient_id→patients, doctor_id→doctors, prescribed_date, valid_until, status, diagnosis_code, diagnosis_description, notes, is_electronic, created_at, updated_at)
  prescription_items(id, prescription_id→prescriptions, drug_id→drugs, quantity_prescribed, dosage_instructions, frequency, duration_days, refills_authorized, refills_remaining, substitution_allowed, special_instructions, created_at, updated_at)
  dispensing_records(id, prescription_item_id→prescription_items, pharmacist_id→pharmacists, inventory_id→inventory, quantity_dispensed, dispensed_at, dispensing_notes, counseling_provided, patient_signature_obtained, total_price, copay_amount, created_at, updated_at)
  refills(id, prescription_item_id→prescription_items, pharmacist_id→pharmacists, dispensing_record_id→dispensing_records, requested_at, approved_at, dispensed_at, status, denial_reason, refill_number, quantity_dispensed, created_at, updated_at)
  insurance_claims(id, dispensing_record_id→dispensing_records, insurance_provider_id→insurance_providers, patient_id→patients, claim_number, submitted_at, processed_at, status, billed_amount, approved_amount, patient_responsibility, rejection_code, rejection_reason, bin_number, pcn_number, created_at, updated_at)

Heuristic pre-classifications:
  drug_categories: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 1 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  dosage_forms: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  manufacturers: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  suppliers: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  drugs: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 3 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  drug_interactions: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 2 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  allergies: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 1 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  insurance_providers: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  patients: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  patient_allergies: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 2 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  doctors: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  pharmacists: dimension (confidence=medium) — No FKs; descriptive entity attributes.
  inventory: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  prescriptions: dimension (confidence=medium) — Has 2 outgoing FK(s), no transaction date; likely snowflake dimension.
  prescription_items: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  dispensing_records: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  refills: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.
  insurance_claims: fact (confidence=high) — Has FKs + date + measures; records a transaction event.

Business context: Database "pharmacy". Domain inferred from table/column names.
